Text: $APLD Very bullish earnings call. Wes expects more than 600 MW online over the next 12 months and another 250 MW of expansion leases signed by year end. On those leases, he’s looking for rent increases ABOVE 15%, possibly with longer terms. This is mega. APLD delivered 250 MW over the past year. Now they expect to deliver more than twice that over the next year. Polaris Forge 1 (Ellendale, ND - AI factory leased to $CRWV) already has 250 MW operating of the 400 MW contracted there. A few other things stood out for me 1. About $36 billion in contracted revenue across five AI factory campuses in 3 states. Approximately $86B if all renewal options are exercised. Polaris Forge 3 (Center, ND AI factory leased to $META) , and Delta Forge 1 and 2 (Boyce, LA and Brookwood, AL AI factory leased to $META) all have the same tier-one investment-grade hyperscaler. We know that hyperscaler is $META from public records although Wes did not confirm it. 2. Construction of all 400 MW at Polaris Forge 1 and the contracted 200 MW at Polaris Forge 2 (Harwood, ND AI factory leased to $ORCL) is fully funded. The latest $1.59B PF1 financing was at 7% interest, compared with 9.25% on the earlier PF1 debt. I like seeing the borrowing costs come down as they prove they can deliver these buildings. 3. They’re working on financing PF3, DF1 and DF2 through Macquarie preferred equity and project debt, with APLD keeping majority ownership. Management sounded confident about the terms it can get with that investment-grade tenant ($META) behind the leases. Those financings still need to close. 4. Base HPC rental income in Q1 was $65.8M, up about 49% in ONE quarter. HPC net operating income was $58.8M, with an 89% margin. And most of the 1.4 GW contracted capacity still has to come online. Adjusted EBITDA was $64.4M, excluding $CHRN. Total revenue was $341.9M, up 322%, including $183.5M of tenant fit-out work. 5. APLD finished the quarter with about $2.95B in cash plus $728M in restricted cash, against roughly $6.4B of debt. More than 80% of debt principal doesn’t mature until fiscal 2031 or later. 6. Wes sees a path to roughly 2 GW operating by the end of 2028 AND 3.5 to 4 GW by the end of 2030 - the second half was NEW news. DF1 is targeting initial operations in the first half of 2027. There is a lot of construction ahead, but we’re starting to see what this company should look like in a few years. 7. APLD signed a power agreement for a planned 1,200 MW gas plant to support PF3 expansion, with deliveries expected from 2030. APLD also owns about 10% of Base Electron. That could give them a lot more room to expandl in North Dakota. 8. Finland gives $APLD access to up to 1 GW of potential power, with initial availability expected in 2028. Limited upfront exposure, and they’re already talking to hyperscalers about the site. They looked at 30-40 sites before choosing this one. 9. Wes said he expects ALL of the big 4 hyperscalers will eventually lease AI factories from $APLD in North Dakota. 10. The more community opposition there is to the datacenters of APLD’s competitors the MORE valuable APLD (with its massive permitted AI factories and low community opposition) becomes. 11. Don’t overlook $CHRN. APLD owns approximately 96%. It has a planned 50 MW Microsoft deployment, and Wes says it’s on track for $1B in annual recurring revenue in 2027. He also sees potential for several hundred MW during 2027 to 28, separate from APLD’s large campuses. 12. To secure the pipeline, $APLD reserved roughly FOUR years of entire factory output from some suppliers. Wes also said the facilities are designed for 30-yyplus years of use and to accommodate changing equipment. 13. The rent increases were probably the most encouraging part of the call for me. If APLD can sign the next leases at the pricing Wes is seeking, while continuing to bring down their financing costs, I think there is a lot more upside here. The big theme of the call was APLD is executing well to turn all of that contracted revenue into real revenue. I still see this as a LONG term investment with the big payoff in 2028 when everything under contract is built and generating revenue. Not financial advice. Everyone must do their own due diligence.
